statement: A counter sits at the point (3, 5) on a grid. It moves 4 squares right and 2 squares down. Where is it now?

choices.misconception: I moved left instead of right, subtracting the 4 rather than adding it.
I moved left and up, reversing both directions.
I swapped the two coordinates round before moving.
I moved up instead of down, adding the 2 rather than subtracting it.

hints: Across changes the first number, up changes the second.
The first coordinate is how far across and the second is how far up. Right adds to the first, down subtracts from the second. Change them one at a time.
Moving 4 right takes 3 to 7. Moving 2 down takes 5 to 3. So the counter is at (7, 3).

solutions.reliable: The first number says how far across, the second how far up. Moving 4 squares right adds 4 to the first: 3 + 4 = 7. Moving 2 squares down subtracts 2 from the second: 5 - 2 = 3. So the counter is at (7, 3). The transferable idea: change one coordinate at a time and say the direction out loud - right adds, left subtracts, up adds, down subtracts.

whyOnTest: Swapping the coordinates or the sign of a direction accounts for almost every lost mark on grid questions.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
